headlines.summary: Qualcomm is trying to move into the data center business, where Nvidia has been the dominant player in the AI boom.
headlines.article_text: Qualcomm issues Amazon warrants to acquire 25 million shares Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Qualcomm said it's working with Amazon across "multiple generations of customized silicon" to help build out AWS' AI infrastructure. The chipmaker is trying to move into the data center business, where Nvidia has been the dominant player in the AI boom. Qualcomm issued warrants to Amazon to acquire 25 million shares. In this article QCOM AMZN Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 4:08 04:08 Qualcomm to build chips for Amazon Squawk on the Street Qualcomm shares rose 3% on Tuesday after the company announced a data center infrastructure partnership with Amazon Web Services, a major win as the chipmaker tries to take on Nvidia in the artificial intelligence market. As part of the agreement, Qualcomm said in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission that it issued warrants to Amazon to acquire 25 million shares in the company at $161.26 apiece for a total investment of $4 billion. According to a press release about the technology pact, Qualcomm is working with Amazon "across multiple generations of customized silicon" to help build out AWS' AI infrastructure, specifically focused on inference. "As AI workloads grow exponentially — driving unprecedented demand for compute, storage, networking and memory bandwidth, and energy-efficient infrastructure — the collaboration brings together Amazon's comprehensive, secure, and price-performant AI infrastructure with Qualcomm Technologies' leadership in power-efficient processing, silicon design and system-level integration," the statement said. Qualcomm is known for making processors that power smartphones and other mobile devices. But the company made a big splash in June, when it revealed a central processing unit for data centers called Dragonfly C1000, and said that Meta would use it when it starts production in 2028. The chipmaker said the new CPU was built for agentic AI and focuses on offering computing performance without using too much power. Qualcomm said at the time that it's targeting $15 billion in data center sales in fiscal 2029, and pointed to a road map for going after the market with several different products, including an AI chip and a product that will tie multiple chips together. Read more CNBC tech news 'Model fatigue' sets in as AI labs race to roll out new versions at frenetic pace Meet the CISO: A new front-line star in the AI cybersecurity war Mistral bags $24 billion valuation as Samsung leads funding for Europe's AI champion TSMC, Samsung commit to ASML's newest chipmaking tools as AI drives demand In teaming up with AWS, Qualcomm is getting a show of confidence from another hyperscaler. Like Meta, Amazon's annual capital expenditures on AI infrastructure are reaching into the hundreds of billions of dollars. Qualcomm's warrant to Amazon expires on Sept. 3, 2036. The company said the shares vest in tranches tied to the "execution of certain commercial arrangements," as well as the purchase of up to $60 billion worth of Qualcomm's server chips and other technology. Nvidia has emerged as the world's most valuable company by dominating the market for graphics processing units, or GPUs, which are needed for building sophisticated AI models and running the heftiest workloads. But more chipmakers are getting involved in the AI boom now that the CPU is proving key for AI. While GPUs are ideal for training and running AI models because they have thousands of tiny cores narrowly focused on performing many operations simultaneously, CPUs have a smaller number of powerful cores running sequential general purpose tasks. Bank of America predicts the CPU market could more than double, from $27 billion in 2025 to $60 billion by 2030. Intel and Advanced Micro Devices are both seeing surging demand for their data center CPUs, and Nvidia in March offered new details about its agentic-optimized CPUs. Dion Harris, Nvidia's head of AI infrastructure, told CNBC at the time that, "CPUs are becoming the bottleneck in terms of growing out this AI and agentic workflow." — CNBC's Katie Tarasov contributed to this report. headlines.summary: Xiaomi and Huawei launched new foldables ahead of Apple’s event, where the company is rumored to unveil its first foldable iPhone.
headlines.article_text: Xiaomi, Huawei take on Apple’s rumored foldable iPhone Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Xiaomi and Huawei launched new foldable smartphones ahead of Apple’s Wednesday event, where the company is rumored to unveil its first foldable iPhone. Apple could ship 6 million foldable iPhones this year and capture 25% of the global foldable smartphone market, according to Counterpoint Research. Apple would face Samsung globally, which dominates the foldable market. In this article 1810-HK AAPL Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 4:36 04:36 New foldable competitors to iPhone: Here's what to know Squawk Box Huawei and Xiaomi this week rolled out their latest foldable phones as the Chinese tech giants look to steal a lead on rival Apple , which is rumored to launch its first foldable iPhone on Wednesday. Xiaomi , the world's third-largest smartphone player, introduced the Xiaomi 18 Fold on Monday, a passport-sized device similar to Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold8, which was released earlier this year . Huawei on Monday unveiled the Mate XT2, the third generation of its trifold smartphone , which it pioneered. Those launches are no coincidence. Apple is holding an event on Wednesday , where it is rumored to be unveiling the first foldable iPhone, a major new product under new CEO John Ternus . "There is significant pent-up demand for a foldable iPhone within the Apple community," Neil Shah, partner at Counterpoint Research, told CNBC on Tuesday. "Many have refrained from switching to Samsung. Some have switched, but they might come back if there is an amazing foldable iPhone." Apple could ship 6 million foldable iPhones this year, giving it a 25% share of the global market, according to Counterpoint Research. This share could grow to 40% in 2027, Counterpoint said. Foldable smartphones continue to see strong growth, even though they are some of the most expensive handsets on the market. Read more CNBC tech news 'Model fatigue' sets in as AI labs race to roll out new versions at frenetic pace Meet the CISO: A new front-line star in the AI cybersecurity war Mistral bags $24 billion valuation as Samsung leads funding for Europe's AI champion TSMC, Samsung commit to ASML's newest chipmaking tools as AI drives demand Globally, Samsung, which pioneered the foldable category with its first such device in 2019, will be Apple's main rival. But in China, Apple will compete against a host of players, led by Huawei, which accounts for more than two-thirds of the foldable market in the country. Shah said "aspiring Chinese consumers" are likely to want Apple's latest device. "We will see lots of upgrades from the existing install base in China happening toward the foldable iPhone," Shah said. After Samsung's latest foldable release in July, there will be plenty of options for consumers to pick from. "This is not an innocent decision by these vendors," Francisco Jeronimo, a vice president at IDC covering mobile devices, told CNBC. "They knew Apple was coming up with a foldable, so they're trying to get ahead and, more importantly, trying to make sure that when the Apple products hit the stores, their product is there so consumers can compare." Huawei and Xiaomi chips Huawei and Xiaomi this week touted their own self-designed chips in their foldables. Xiaomi said the Xiaomi 18 Fold is powered by the XRing O3, its latest smartphone processor, manufactured on an advanced process.
